sources.abstract: [0000]    A system and method for performing automated software code reviews using agentic artificial intelligence (AI), comprising a code ingestion module for receiving code changesets from source control systems, an agentic AI module that autonomously plans and orchestrates review workflows by selectively invoking external analysis tools and optional sub-agent modules based on contextual metadata and repository-specific configuration, a hierarchical configuration subsystem customizable per-repository, per-organization, per-team, or per-user, and a feedback delivery engine for transmitting structured, context-sensitive review feedback in natural language through inline repository comments, command-line interfaces, email, or application programming interfaces.

sources.title: SYSTEM FOR NORMALIZED WORKFLOW MAPPING AND DYNAMIC AGENT DEPLOYMENT IN DISTRIBUTED COMPUTING ENVIRONMENTS [US20260349909A1]
sources.abstract: A system and method are disclosed for comparative task execution analysis between human personnel and AI agents. The system provides a graphical user interface configured to render task indicators corresponding to a plurality of tasks, each task associated with a first task execution record and a second task execution record. The first task execution record reflects execution of subtasks by personnel within an organizational hierarchy, while the second task execution record reflects execution of corresponding subtasks by AI agents. Through the interface, a user may select tasks, view hierarchical decompositions into subtasks, and identify which human personnel or AI agent executed each subtask. The system may receive user input linking human-executed subtasks with candidate AI agents, enabling simulation of modified task executions and visual comparison of resource substitution scenarios. The system may further display real-time execution telemetry, input-output mappings, and performance metrics for both human personnel and AI agents.

sources.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AGENTS BUILDING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AGENTS [US20260349665A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    In an example embodiment, an AI agent is provided that builds other AI agents. More specifically, the AI agent is designed to conduct an interview with a human in a manner that extracts contextual and domain knowledge regarding one or more tasks to be performed in an organization. The AI agent may then use this extracted knowledge to create one or more AI agents to actually perform the tasks of the organization.

sources.title: System and Method for Dynamic Workspace Orchestration [US20260350144A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A method, computer program product, and computer system for processing a request for a secure dynamic workspace in a cloud computing environment. In response to processing the request, the secure dynamic workspace is generated in the cloud computing environment by provisioning a plurality of cloud computing resources for use within the secure dynamic workspace. One or more artificial intelligence (AI) agents are deployed within the secure dynamic workspace using the plurality of cloud computing resources. One or more interactions with the one or more AI agents are processed using content information defined within the secure dynamic workspace. A state for the one or more AI agents is managed within secure dynamic workspace based upon, at least in part, the one or more interactions.

sources.title: Dynamic Orchestration of Multi-Agent AI Workflows [US20260349805A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A method includes receiving a user query and determining a first agentic task of a plurality of agentic tasks to perform based on the user query. The method includes selecting a first AI agent from a plurality of AI agents based on the first agentic task and performing the first agentic task using the first AI agent. Based on the user query and performance of the first agentic task, the method includes determining a second agentic task of the plurality of agentic tasks to perform. The method includes selecting a second AI agent based on the second agentic task from the plurality of AI agents and performing the second agentic task using the second AI agent.

sources.title: AGENTIC-AI DRIVEN DYNAMIC COMPOSITION OF ANALYTIC ARTIFACTS IN A COMPOSABLE PLATFORM [US20260350420A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A method in a composable platform architecture, comprising: deriving constraints and constructing a feature set from one or more qualified trigger events; traversing a knowledge graph representing interconnected modular assets to identify one or more assets based on the derived constraints and constructed feature set; composing an analytic artifact based on the identified assets, wherein the analytic artifact comprises a decisioning artifact, an optimization artifact, or a simulation artifact; executing the composed analytic artifact to simulate an outcome; and generating a recommendation based on the outcome.

sources.title: PRIVACY PRESERVING EDGE-CLOUD COLLABORATION FOR EMBODIED AI AGENTS [US20260349798A1]
sources.abstract: In one implementation, a device makes a classification of sensor data captured by an embodied agent. The device selects, based on the classification of the sensor data, between storing the sensor data in a local memory in a local network of the embodied agent or in a cloud memory in a cloud location. The device makes a classification of a subtask of a task to be performed by the embodied agent. The device selects, based on the classification of the subtask, whether the subtask is to be performed in the local network using the local memory or in the cloud location using the cloud memory.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Framework for Scalable Task Performance [US20260350511A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Embodiments are provided that include (i) receiving a natural language request to perform a task; (ii) in response to receiving the request, generating, by a first AI agent, a flow based on a representation of a subset of capabilities; (iii) providing the flow to a second AI agent; and (iv) executing, by the second AI agent, the flow in order to perform the task. The second AI agent can then execute capabilities of the flow by (i) deterministically executing capabilities that are likely to achieve success when executed in that manner, and/or (ii) providing capabilities that are less likely to achieve success when executed deterministically to a third AI agent (e.g., a multi-modal model) to execute the capabilities, with the success or failure of a capability assessed by the second AI agent regardless of the method used to execute the capability.

sources.title: Unified Valuation Framework (UVF) for Adaptive Decision Optimization in Autonomous and Distributed Systems [US20260350405A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    The Unified Valuation Framework (UVF) provides a modular optimization structure enabling autonomous agents and distributed systems to dynamically optimize cumulative operational value by balancing opportunity capture, future potential, environmental coordination, operational costs, and continuity risks. The framework employs a tunable, multi-dimensional valuation function that adaptively reweights decision criteria in real time, supporting optimization across dynamic, adversarial, stochastic, and cooperative environments. A formal optimization theorem demonstrates that UVF agents statistically outperform purely greedy agents under specified adversarial conditions. Unlike reinforcement learning (RL) or Markov Decision Process (MDP) models, UVF does not require episodic training, value iteration, or policy convergence, and instead enables context-sensitive action selection using localized environmental feedback. This supports adaptive optimization in safety-critical, adversarial, or resource-constrained domains, including but not limited to military autonomy, financial trading, disaster response, cloud resource management, resilient transportation, AI planning under uncertainty, and autonomous space exploration.

sources.title: AGENTIC ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ONLINE CHECKOUT [WO2026231659A1]
sources.abstract: Systems and methods for secure agentic checkout transactions are disclosed. A checkout facilitator system may retrieve merchant metadata, generate an agentic schema comprising facilitator identity, cardholder verification information, and transaction metadata, and transmit the agentic schema to a merchant system during an online checkout session. The checkout facilitator system may also generate a transaction token based on cryptographic credentials provisioned during enrollment and embed the transaction token and a payment token into a checkout payload. The merchant system may validate the agentic schema and forward the checkout payload for authorization. A computer system operated by a payment network may provision tokens, generate cryptographic credentials, and validate transaction tokens during processing. The systems described enable autonomous agents, virtual assistants, or smart devices to securely complete purchases on behalf of users while preserving transaction integrity, authentication assurance, and merchant visibility.

sources.title: PRIVACY-SAFE IDENTIFIERS FOR USING GENERATIVE AI AGENTS IN GROUP CHATS [US20260352614A1]
sources.abstract: The described techniques provide a framework interfacing between chats and the AI engine that anonymizes the user identities in messages that are shared with an AI engine to generate response messages, and then re-introducing user names back into the response messages. Disclosed embodiments include, (a) during pre-AI processing time, identifying and replacing “@mention-personally identifiable information” with a unique identifier in a message, before being processed by the AI engine. Then, (b) during a post-AI processing time, recovering, from the AI engine output, the “@mention-personally identifiable information” based on the unique identifier and present that output with the “@mention-personally identifiable information” as a response message to the chat thread of the original message. Such mechanisms may include techniques for anonymization, abstraction, or structural input design that preserves conversational context without exposing personal identities.

sources.title: IDENTITY SECURITY FOR ROBOTS AND AI AGENTS PARTICIPATING IN A COLLABORATION SESSION [US20260352505A1]
sources.abstract: A system implements techniques for executing a collaboration session between at least one human participant, at least one robotic device participant, and at least one artificial intelligence agent participant. One particular challenge encountered when executing the collaboration session, or preparing to execute the collaboration session, relates to identity security. The disclosed system uses an identity platform to implement security measures for participants in relation to a collaboration session. For example, via the use of participant identifiers and the identity platform, the system determines if and/or how individual participants are authorized to join a collaboration session. In another example, via the use of participant identifiers and the identity platform, the system determines which functions participants are authorized to implement within a context of the collaboration session.

sources.title: DYNAMIC MULTI-AGENT FRAMEWORK FOR UNSTRUCTURED DATA EXTRACTION, NORMALIZATION, AND VALIDATION [US20260350354A1]
sources.abstract: A hierarchical multi-agent system processes unstructured data through coordinated operation of specialized artificial intelligence agents. An orchestrator agent dynamically allocates processing tasks across extractor agents, formatter agents, quality assurance agents, and knowledge base agents based on computational requirements. The extractor agents implement parallel processing pipelines to identify and extract data elements from unstructured input including scanned documents, handwritten notes, and multilingual text. The formatter agents transform extracted data into structured formats according to predefined schemas. The quality assurance agents validate transformed data against configurable accuracy thresholds. The knowledge base agents categorize and validate extracted information using domain-specific knowledge bases that expand through automated learning. The system implements cross-model verification between multiple large language models, operating in a distributed computing environment with dynamic task allocation and automated optimization protocols.

sources.title: SYSTEM FOR DETECTION AND REMEDIATION OF SECURITY CONFIGURATION DRIFTS IN WEB APPLICATIONS USING INTERFACE-CENTRIC AI AGENTS [US20260350240A1]
sources.abstract: A computer-implemented technique for automated compliance verification and remediation of interface elements in a graphical user interface of a web application is disclosed. A language model determines, for each interface element associated with a security configuration setting, a first compliance state based on on-screen textual content visible at runtime. For interface elements identified as non-compliant with a predefined security baseline, a configuration state is altered through simulated user interaction. A second compliance state is determined from updated on-screen textual content produced in response to the simulated interaction, and the altered interface element is confirmed against an expected compliant configuration. The technique further supports generation of verification failure alerts and tamper-evident audit records. The approach accommodates dynamic interface changes and enables periodic compliance enforcement across multiple web applications, thereby improving consistency, auditability, and reliability of security configuration management.

sources.title: DYNAMIC LATTICE-BASED EXECUTION FRAMEWORK FOR DISTRIBUTED AI AGENTS [EP4835666A1]
sources.abstract: A system and method for orchestrating execution of interdependent decision-making subtasks using a plurality of AI agents. The system receives, from an endpoint device, a task comprising a task context that includes a decision objective and associated data references. An execution graph is generated defining a plurality of subtasks and inter-subtask dependencies. A corresponding AI agent is instantiated for each subtask, with a dynamically scoped task context and constrained data access. Each AI agent executes its assigned subtask based on the scoped context, producing structured outputs. The system then determines target locations within a structured output template for each subtask output using semantic identifiers, positional metadata, and execution graph dependencies. The system inserts the outputs into their mapped locations to synthesize a final decision artifact.

sources.title: SYSTEM FOR NORMALIZED WORKFLOW MAPPING AND DYNAMIC AGENT DEPLOYMENT IN DISTRIBUTED COMPUTING ENVIRONMENTS [EP4835667A1]
sources.abstract: A system and method are disclosed for comparative task execution analysis between human personnel and AI agents. The system provides a graphical user interface configured to render task indicators corresponding to a plurality of tasks, each task associated with a first task execution record and a second task execution record. The first task execution record reflects execution of subtasks by personnel within an organizational hierarchy, while the second task execution record reflects execution of corresponding subtasks by AI agents. Through the interface, a user may select tasks, view hierarchical decompositions into subtasks, and identify which human personnel or AI agent executed each subtask. The system may receive user input linking human-executed subtasks with candidate AI agents, enabling simulation of modified task executions and visual comparison of resource substitution scenarios. The system may further display real-time execution telemetry, input-output mappings, and performance metrics for both human personnel and AI agents.

sources.title: KNOWLEDGE GRAPH POWERED, AGENTIC AI GUIDED RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED GENERATION [US20260339932A1]
sources.abstract: An intelligent query augmentation agentic AI system leveraging a knowledge graph for one or more knowledge domains has been created. The knowledge graph has been built to indicate entities and relationships among those entities based on defined taxonomy and ontology. The agentic AI system includes an orchestrator and one or more additional AI agents. The orchestrator extracts entities from the received query and directs the AI agent(s) to obtain information about the extracted entities. The orchestrator interacts with a requestor-context AI agent that collects information on activities of the requestor. The orchestrator also interacts with an organization-context AI agent that searches data sources for information related to the extracted entities. The orchestrator queries the graph based on the collected information and a degree of relationship. The agentic AI system augments the received query with the graph structured data and communicates the query to a target AI model.

sources.title: AI Agents for Supply Chain Code of Conduct Compliance [US20260340650A1]
sources.organization: CUOMO GENNARO ANTHONY, ADIVI SHYAM, SRIDHAR PALGHAT KRISHNAN
sources.abstract: A system for automated supplier Code of Conduct (CoC) compliance assessment is disclosed. The system dynamically discovers, extracts, and analyzes supplier CoC policies using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ensure assessments are based on real-world documents. It employs large language model (LLM)-generated AI agents instantiated in real time, each assigned specific roles and tasks corresponding to compliance disciplines such as labor rights, environmental practices, and anti-corruption. The agents operate in structured squads, executing tasks in defined sequences with self-reflection to refine outputs. Compliance alignment is measured using similarity scoring, and the system triggers automated actions—such as alerts or corrective requests—when policy gaps are detected. A persistent compliance store retains all results for auditability and ongoing governance. The invention enables scalable, real-time, and transparent compliance monitoring with minimal human intervention, improving accuracy, efficiency, and supplier accountability in supply chain operations.

draft.summary: Research output on AI agents has grown very fast: OpenAlex works rose from 1,689 in 2024 to 8,202 in 2025, and the year-to-date count is 28,119 against 5,317 a year earlier. Patent publications show a similar rise, but are partly undercounted by publication delay and are claims, not proof. Several large and mid-size software vendors say in SEC filings that they ship agent products (M1, M2, M3, M5, M6). Filings also treat agents mainly as a risk vector rather than a proven revenue source (M8, M9). The research literature itself points to immature reliability evidence. Success-only evaluation can hide process failures, and many safety and governance proposals are conceptual with no empirical validation (R1, R7, C4, C6). Main uncertainty: whether agents become dependable enough for broad, autonomous commercial use. The evidence contains no agent-specific revenue, customer-count or independent adoption data. Research volume is not commercial success.
draft.plain_summary: AI agents are software programs that can carry out tasks on their own, such as setting up IT accounts or handling invoices. Research and patent filings on them are growing very fast, and several well-known software companies say they are selling agent products. The thing that could stop it is reliability and trust: studies show agents can make hidden mistakes or be steered into bad choices, and companies themselves warn about this.
